explanation: A satellite in low orbit laps Earth about every 90 minutes, yet Earth carries it, and us, around the Sun nearly four times faster, covering about 2.6 million km a day.

issues.note: Without a named measure, faster is frame-dependent: relative to the Sun a low-orbit satellite moves at Earth's 29.8 km/s plus or minus its own 7.7 km/s, so it is sometimes faster than Earth. The labels (in low Earth orbit, in its orbit round the Sun) point to orbital speeds and the measure field says orbital speed, but the measure is not shipped to players (ARCHITECTURE 5.1.1). A stem such as Which has the higher orbital speed? would close the reading.
